nodes.name: Closed-Loop Fluid Recovery & Regeneration
nodes.description: Captures, purifies, and continuously recirculates the wash fluid or cleaning medium to drastically reduce fresh water input.
idea_text: A specialized tumbling drum system where clothes are cleaned with a mixture of tiny, reusable cryogel granules. These granules gently abrade the fabric, absorbing oils, dirt, and odor molecules. After the cycle, the granules are separated from the clothes, cleaned (e.g., by vacuuming or solvent bath), and reused, with no water used in the garment cleaning process itself.

A laundry drum or chamber equipped with high-efficiency vacuum nozzles and brushes. Clothes are tumbled while a powerful vacuum system actively lifts and extracts dust, lint, pet hair, and superficial dry dirt from the fabric. This process also helps remove airborne particles and can extend the life of garments between full wet washes.

A home appliance that uses recycled supercritical CO2 as the primary cleaning agent. Clothes are placed in a sealed chamber, CO2 is pressurized to its supercritical state, dissolves dirt, then is depressurized back to a gas for collection and reuse.

An advanced washing machine that incorporates an electrocoagulation system into its water purification loop. After a minimal initial wash with water, the greywater is treated with electrocoagulation to rapidly aggregate and remove dirt, dyes, and other contaminants. This pre-treatment significantly reduces the load on subsequent filtration, allowing the water to be recycled and reused much more efficiently for consecutive washes, minimizing fresh water intake.

A specialized laundry chamber or drum designed with precisely positioned nozzles that generate high-velocity, controlled air vortices around and through the garments. These aerodynamic forces would gently lift and carry away dry dust, lint, pet hair, and superficial particulate dirt from fabric fibers, collecting them in a filter system, effectively de-soiling clothes without any water.

Develop a cleaning system that introduces microscopic, fabric-safe magnetic particles (e.g., in a fine mist or dry powder form) engineered to selectively adhere to dirt, oils, and odor-causing compounds on garments. After a brief tumbling period to ensure contact, a powerful, oscillating magnetic field is applied to pull these dirt-laden magnetic particles out of the fabric and into a collection chamber for separation and potential reuse.

Design a cleaning chamber where clothes are gently suspended in a minimal volume of water or a specialized, low-surface-tension cleaning solution. A system of diffusers beneath the garments introduces precisely controlled, pulsed streams of fine air or inert gas bubbles. These bubbles percolate through the fabric, creating a gentle "scrubbing" action that dislodges dirt and impurities, which are then collected from the circulating minimal liquid.

A specialized washing unit where clothes are suspended in a minimal amount of slightly conductive water or a weak electrolyte solution. The chamber incorporates alternating cation and anion exchange membranes. By applying an electric current, charged dirt particles (ions) and dissolved impurities are drawn out of the fabric and across the membranes, leaving cleaner fabric and significantly purified water for near-complete reuse within the closed system.

Develop cleaning agents or fabric coatings containing embedded or surface-applied smart polymers. When triggered (e.g., by a slight temperature change or pH adjustment in a low-humidity chamber with minimal mist), these polymers swell, physically pushing dirt and grime out of the fabric pores. Upon a reverse trigger, they contract, squeezing out any trapped impurities or dirty water, which is then collected, significantly reducing water usage for cleaning and rinsing.

A washing device featuring a textured internal surface or specialized micro-channels. Garments are laid flat or gently rolled across this surface while a very thin, continuously flowing film of water or cleaning solution is introduced. The micro-scale geometry of the surface generates localized fluid shear forces that effectively "peel" and dislodge surface dirt and oils from the fabric with an extremely low volume of liquid, which is then filtered and recirculated.

A compact garment cleaning appliance that uses a targeted, re-circulating vapor of a fabric-safe, low-boiling-point solvent (e.g., a modified alcohol or fluorocarbon). Clothes, or specific stained areas, are exposed to this vapor. The vapor condenses on the cooler fabric, dissolves oils and grime, and then re-evaporates, carrying the contaminants away to a recovery and purification system, leaving no residue and requiring no water for the cleaning process.

A sealed garment cabinet containing regenerable desiccant materials (e.g., advanced zeolites or MOFs) and a fan. Air is circulated through the garments and then over the desiccant bed. The desiccant actively pulls moisture (and dissolved body oils/odors) directly from the fabric into the air stream, and then adsorbs it. This dry extraction process cleanses and deodorizes garments without the use of water. The desiccant can then be heated to release the dirty moisture for disposal and regenerate for reuse.

A system where garments are briefly immersed in a minimal volume of a low-viscosity, fabric-safe MR fluid. A pulsed magnetic field is then applied, causing the fluid to momentarily thicken around the fabric fibers, effectively encapsulating and mechanically stressing embedded dirt and oil particles. When the field is removed, the fluid instantly thins, releasing the loosened dirt, which is then carried away by filtration. The fluid is continuously recycled and purified for subsequent uses with minimal loss and no water.

A specialized, highly reusable sheet or pad made from a superhydrophilic, finely textured material designed to be placed in a tumbling dryer or a dedicated refresh cabinet with clothes. During a brief cycle with a very fine, minimal mist of water, this sheet actively attracts and captures body oils, dissolved dirt, and fine particulate matter released from the garments. The superhydrophilic material "wicks" and holds these contaminants, effectively cleaning the clothes with minimal water, and the sheet is then rinsed clean for reuse.

A controlled chamber system that applies a fine, non-toxic, biodegradable, and fabric-safe "bio-slime" (e.g., a hydrogel-based polymer with specific adhesive properties) mist onto clothes. This slime is engineered to be slightly adhesive to dirt and odor molecules. After a short dwell time, a second stage triggers a controlled 'shedding' or breakdown of the slime (e.g., via a pH change or mild vibration), causing it to detach from the fabric, carrying the trapped dirt and odors with it, into a collection system. The slime is then processed for disposal or regeneration, leaving clean, residue-free clothes with minimal water usage.

A sealed laundry cabinet that cleans and refreshes clothes using a fine mist of water combined with eco-friendly cleaning agents. The mist humidifies and helps release dirt particles, which are then condensed, collected, and filtered, effectively cleaning with very low water usage per cycle.

A minimal-water wash system where clothes are immersed in a very small volume of water containing a low concentration of cleaning agents. High-frequency acoustic transducers are precisely arrayed to generate acoustic radiation forces that gently 'push' and aggregate dirt particles within the water towards a specific collection zone or filter, without requiring bulk fluid flow or mechanical agitation of the clothes. This allows for highly efficient dirt removal from the water, enabling near-complete water recirculation and minimal fresh water input for effective cleaning.

A washing machine integrated with a membrane distillation unit. After an initial minimal-water wash, the greywater is fed into the membrane distillation system. Water vapor passes through the hydrophobic membrane, leaving all dissolved and suspended contaminants in the concentrated brine. This purified water is then condensed and immediately recycled for the next wash cycle, achieving ultra-high water recovery and significantly reducing fresh water intake.

A garment refreshing cabinet that utilizes a bed of regenerable, fabric-safe chemical sorbents (e.g., modified amines or Metal-Organic Frameworks). These sorbents are specifically engineered to reversibly bind volatile organic compounds (VOCs) responsible for odors. Air is circulated through the garments and then over the sorbent bed, trapping odors. The sorbent is then periodically regenerated (e.g., by heating or pressure swing), releasing concentrated odors for safe disposal, making this a highly efficient, water-free, and chemical-free deodorization system.

A garment cleaning system where a very fine, dry, and biodegradable micro-abrasive powder (e.g., cellulose beads) is gently dusted onto clothes. A precisely controlled, low-power pulsed laser beam then scans the fabric. The laser energy interacts with the micro-abrasive particles, causing them to gently 'lift' or 'etch' away dirt and grime from the fabric surface through localized photomechanical action. The dirty micro-abrasive is then vacuumed away, providing a contactless, water-free cleaning method.

A sealed chamber where garments are exposed to a precise, low-temperature, recycled carrier gas containing a non-toxic, fabric-safe binding agent. This agent selectively vaporizes, diffuses into the fabric, adsorbs to dirt and odor molecules, and then is carried away by the gas stream to a separation and recovery unit. The carrier gas and binding agent are continuously purified and reused, effectively "chromatographically eluting" dirt and odors from the fabric without water.

A laundry appliance featuring a series of rotating polymer rollers whose surfaces are engineered to have a higher affinity for common dirt and oil molecules than for fabric fibers. As garments pass through, these rollers gently contact the fabric, transferring dirt and oils from the clothes onto their own surfaces. A secondary, integrated mechanism continuously cleans the rollers (e.g., with a scraper or micro-solvent spray which is then recovered), enabling continuous dirt removal from clothes without water.

A low-water washing system that uses a mild, biodegradable solution containing engineered humic acid analogues or naturally derived humic substances. These compounds act as powerful chelating and dispersing agents, effectively binding to dirt, oils, and metal ions embedded in fabric. This complexation process makes the contaminants easier to rinse away with a minimal amount of water, which is then purified and recycled through a system optimized to separate the humic-dirt complexes.

A sealed garment cabinet that uses a small, contained reservoir of water. This water is rapidly heated to generate superheated, dry steam (vapor without liquid droplets). This superheated steam is circulated through the garments, effectively sterilizing, deodorizing, and loosening superficial dirt and oils through thermal shock and vapor action. The steam then cools, condenses, and is immediately collected, filtered, and returned to the reservoir for continuous reuse, achieving powerful cleaning with extremely low water replenishment.

Garments are treated with a dissolvable or detachable nanocoating that has a stronger affinity for dirt/oils than for fabric fibers. After wear, the garments are placed in a gentle tumbling drum or cabinet. A mild, fabric-safe trigger (e.g., a specific light wavelength, a slight humidity change, or a very mild vibration) causes the nanocoating to rapidly delaminate or de-bond from the fabric, encapsulating and releasing the accumulated dirt. The shed nanocoating and dirt particles are then collected by a vacuum and filter system, leaving clean fabric with no water.

A washing machine integrated with a forward osmosis system. After an initial, minimal-water wash cycle, the greywater (feed solution) is pumped to one side of an FO membrane. A highly concentrated, reusable draw solution is on the other side. Clean water is naturally pulled from the greywater through the membrane, leaving all contaminants and dirt in the concentrated feed solution, and the purified water is then recycled back into the wash system for continuous reuse, drastically reducing fresh water consumption.

A garment refreshing cabinet where an internal electric field generates a controlled "ion wind" or electrohydrodynamic flow. This silent, gentle, localized air current is directed across the fabric surfaces, physically dislodging dry dust, lint, and carrying away odor molecules without any moving mechanical parts. The dislodged particles and odors are then collected by an integrated filter and purification system, providing a water-free and gentle cleaning method.

A sealed laundry chamber where garments are held taut. A system of micro-nozzles precisely injects localized micro-bursts of a fabric-safe, miscible, low-boiling-point solvent (in its gas phase) directly into the fabric weave. This gaseous solvent deeply penetrates and dissolves hydrophobic dirt and oils. A gentle, continuous vacuum then pulls the dirt-laden gas out, which is subsequently condensed, purified, and recycled for continuous reuse, providing highly targeted and water-free cleaning.

A low-water washing system that utilizes a highly concentrated, yet gentle, biodegradable biosurfactant foam. Garments are placed in a chamber where a precise, minimal amount of water, cleaning agents, and biosurfactant is agitated to create a dense, stable foam. Clothes are gently tumbled through this foam, allowing the biosurfactants to lift and emulsify dirt with minimal bulk water. The foam is then collapsed, and the concentrated dirty liquid is filtered and recycled, or collected for disposal, significantly reducing water volume.

A garment cleaning system that employs a fine mist of water containing specialized, fabric-safe, marine-derived or inspired chelating agents. These agents are designed to selectively bind to metallic ions, mineral deposits (e.g., from hard water stains), and certain organic pollutants commonly found in dirt and stains. Once chelated, the contaminants become more soluble or easily dislodged, allowing for effective removal with significantly reduced water rinsing, which is then filtered to remove the chelated compounds for safe disposal or recovery.

A low-water garment cleaning chamber where clothes are immersed in a minimal volume of specialized, mildly aqueous solution. Fine, microscopic air bubbles are then introduced into the solution. These bubbles are engineered to selectively adhere to hydrophobic dirt, oils, and grease particles embedded in the fabric. The dirt-laden bubbles rise to the surface, forming a stable "froth" that is continuously skimmed off and filtered, effectively extracting contaminants from the garments with extremely low water usage and minimal mechanical agitation. The cleaned water is then recirculated.

A sealed laundry drum lined with or containing pellets of a durable, fabric-safe solid catalyst (e.g., a noble metal or metal oxide catalyst). Clothes are tumbled in a precisely controlled, slightly humid or dry atmosphere containing a gentle oxidant (e.g., low concentration ozone or peroxide vapor). The catalyst promotes the gentle oxidation and breakdown of organic dirt, body oils, and odor molecules into simpler, volatile compounds (like CO2 and water vapor), which are then vented and filtered. This provides a dry, continuous, and chemical-free deep cleaning with no water requirement for the actual cleaning.

A washing machine with an integrated, ultra-efficient closed-loop water purification system. After each wash cycle, the greywater undergoes micro-filtration, reverse osmosis, and UV sterilization, making it pristine and immediately reusable for the next load, virtually eliminating water discharge and demand.

A dry or minimal-mist garment cleaning system that introduces a fine, fabric-safe ferrofluid mist onto clothes. This ferrofluid is engineered to preferentially bind to or encapsulate dirt and oil particles. After a brief dwell time, a localized, oscillating magnetic field is applied. This causes the dirt-laden ferrofluid to be agitated, moved, and then drawn out of the fabric by the magnetic field onto a collection surface, or into a separation chamber, effectively extracting dirt without bulk water. The ferrofluid can then be regenerated and reused.

A closed-loop, high-pressure cleaning chamber that exposes garments to a minimal amount of near-critical water (e.g., 250-350 °C, 5-15 MPa). In this state, water effectively dissolves and cleanses organic dirt, oils, and greases from fabric fibers without harsh detergents. After a short cycle, the system rapidly cools and depressurizes the water, causing contaminants to precipitate out for easy filtration and removal. The purified water is then recycled, achieving powerful cleaning with dramatically reduced water consumption and no chemical discharge.

The sorbent is then periodically regenerated (e.g., by heating or pressure swing), releasing concentrated odors for safe disposal, making this a highly efficient, water-free, and chemical-free deodorization system.

A garment cleaning system where a very fine, dry, and biodegradable micro-abrasive powder (e.g., cellulose beads) is gently dusted onto clothes. A precisely controlled, low-power pulsed laser beam then scans the fabric. The laser energy interacts with the micro-abrasive particles, causing them to gently 'lift' or 'etch' away dirt and grime from the fabric surface through localized photomechanical action. The dirty micro-abrasive is then vacuumed away, providing a contactless, water-free cleaning method.

A sealed chamber where garments are exposed to a precise, low-temperature, recycled carrier gas containing a non-toxic, fabric-safe binding agent. This agent selectively vaporizes, diffuses into the fabric, adsorbs to dirt and odor molecules, and then is carried away by the gas stream to a separation and recovery unit. The carrier gas and binding agent are continuously purified and reused, effectively "chromatographically eluting" dirt and odors from the fabric without water.

A laundry appliance featuring a series of rotating polymer rollers whose surfaces are engineered to have a higher affinity for common dirt and oil molecules than for fabric fibers. As garments pass through, these rollers gently contact the fabric, transferring dirt and oils from the clothes onto their own surfaces. A secondary, integrated mechanism continuously cleans the rollers (e.g., with a scraper or micro-solvent spray which is then recovered), enabling continuous dirt removal from clothes without water.

A low-water washing system that uses a mild, biodegradable solution containing engineered humic acid analogues or naturally derived humic substances. These compounds act as powerful chelating and dispersing agents, effectively binding to dirt, oils, and metal ions embedded in fabric. This complexation process makes the contaminants easier to rinse away with a minimal amount of water, which is then purified and recycled through a system optimized to separate the humic-dirt complexes.

A sealed garment cabinet that uses a small, contained reservoir of water. This water is rapidly heated to generate superheated, dry steam (vapor without liquid droplets). This superheated steam is circulated through the garments, effectively sterilizing, deodorizing, and loosening superficial dirt and oils through thermal shock and vapor action. The steam then cools, condenses, and is immediately collected, filtered, and returned to the reservoir for continuous reuse, achieving powerful cleaning with extremely low water replenishment.

Garments are treated with a dissolvable or detachable nanocoating that has a stronger affinity for dirt/oils than for fabric fibers. After wear, the garments are placed in a gentle tumbling drum or cabinet. A mild, fabric-safe trigger (e.g., a specific light wavelength, a slight humidity change, or a very mild vibration) causes the nanocoating to rapidly delaminate or de-bond from the fabric, encapsulating and releasing the accumulated dirt. The shed nanocoating and dirt particles are then collected by a vacuum and filter system, leaving clean fabric with no water.

A washing machine integrated with a forward osmosis system. After an initial, minimal-water wash cycle, the greywater (feed solution) is pumped to one side of an FO membrane. A highly concentrated, reusable draw solution is on the other side. Clean water is naturally pulled from the greywater through the membrane, leaving all contaminants and dirt in the concentrated feed solution, and the purified water is then recycled back into the wash system for continuous reuse, drastically reducing fresh water consumption.

A garment refreshing cabinet where an internal electric field generates a controlled "ion wind" or electrohydrodynamic flow. This silent, gentle, localized air current is directed across the fabric surfaces, physically dislodging dry dust, lint, and carrying away odor molecules without any moving mechanical parts. The dislodged particles and odors are then collected by an integrated filter and purification system, providing a water-free and gentle cleaning method.

A sealed laundry chamber where garments are held taut. A system of micro-nozzles precisely injects localized micro-bursts of a fabric-safe, miscible, low-boiling-point solvent (in its gas phase) directly into the fabric weave. This gaseous solvent deeply penetrates and dissolves hydrophobic dirt and oils. A gentle, continuous vacuum then pulls the dirt-laden gas out, which is subsequently condensed, purified, and recycled for continuous reuse, providing highly targeted and water-free cleaning.

A low-water washing system that utilizes a highly concentrated, yet gentle, biodegradable biosurfactant foam. Garments are placed in a chamber where a precise, minimal amount of water, cleaning agents, and biosurfactant is agitated to create a dense, stable foam. Clothes are gently tumbled through this foam, allowing the biosurfactants to lift and emulsify dirt with minimal bulk water. The foam is then collapsed, and the concentrated dirty liquid is filtered and recycled, or collected for disposal, significantly reducing water volume.

A garment cleaning system that employs a fine mist of water containing specialized, fabric-safe, marine-derived or inspired chelating agents. These agents are designed to selectively bind to metallic ions, mineral deposits (e.g., from hard water stains), and certain organic pollutants commonly found in dirt and stains. Once chelated, the contaminants become more soluble or easily dislodged, allowing for effective removal with significantly reduced water rinsing, which is then filtered to remove the chelated compounds for safe disposal or recovery.

A low-water garment cleaning chamber where clothes are immersed in a minimal volume of specialized, mildly aqueous solution. Fine, microscopic air bubbles are then introduced into the solution. These bubbles are engineered to selectively adhere to hydrophobic dirt, oils, and grease particles embedded in the fabric. The dirt-laden bubbles rise to the surface, forming a stable "froth" that is continuously skimmed off and filtered, effectively extracting contaminants from the garments with extremely low water usage and minimal mechanical agitation. The cleaned water is then recirculated.

A sealed laundry drum lined with or containing pellets of a durable, fabric-safe solid catalyst (e.g., a noble metal or metal oxide catalyst). Clothes are tumbled in a precisely controlled, slightly humid or dry atmosphere containing a gentle oxidant (e.g., low concentration ozone or peroxide vapor). The catalyst promotes the gentle oxidation and breakdown of organic dirt, body oils, and odor molecules into simpler, volatile compounds (like CO2 and water vapor), which are then vented and filtered. This provides a dry, continuous, and chemical-free deep cleaning with no water requirement for the actual cleaning.

A washing machine with an integrated, ultra-efficient closed-loop water purification system. After each wash cycle, the greywater undergoes micro-filtration, reverse osmosis, and UV sterilization, making it pristine and immediately reusable for the next load, virtually eliminating water discharge and demand.

A dry or minimal-mist garment cleaning system that introduces a fine, fabric-safe ferrofluid mist onto clothes. This ferrofluid is engineered to preferentially bind to or encapsulate dirt and oil particles. After a brief dwell time, a localized, oscillating magnetic field is applied. This causes the dirt-laden ferrofluid to be agitated, moved, and then drawn out of the fabric by the magnetic field onto a collection surface, or into a separation chamber, effectively extracting dirt without bulk water. The ferrofluid can then be regenerated and reused.

A closed-loop, high-pressure cleaning chamber that exposes garments to a minimal amount of near-critical water (e.g., 250-350 °C, 5-15 MPa). In this state, water effectively dissolves and cleanses organic dirt, oils, and greases from fabric fibers without harsh detergents. After a short cycle, the system rapidly cools and depressurizes the water, causing contaminants to precipitate out for easy filtration and removal. The purified water is then recycled, achieving powerful cleaning with dramatically reduced water consumption and no chemical discharge.

included_members.idea_text: A home appliance that uses recycled supercritical CO2 as the primary cleaning agent. Clothes are placed in a sealed chamber, CO2 is pressurized to its supercritical state, dissolves dirt, then is depressurized back to a gas for collection and reuse.
included_members.abstraction: Closed-loop solvent recovery and purification: A recirculating fluid-management subsystem that captures used cleaning solvent (vapor and/or liquid), separates and removes contaminants, restores solvent quality via regeneration, and returns it to the cleaning process to minimize fresh solvent and water demand.

included_members.explanation: M57 explicitly describes closed-loop solvent recovery and purification, perfectly matching Closed-Loop Fluid Recovery & Regeneration.

included_members.idea_text: A sealed laundry cabinet that cleans and refreshes clothes using a fine mist of water combined with eco-friendly cleaning agents. The mist humidifies and helps release dirt particles, which are then condensed, collected, and filtered, effectively cleaning with very low water usage per cycle.
included_members.abstraction: Aerosol cleaning with moisture capture and recycling: Use a fine airborne moisture phase to mobilize and lift soil from textiles, then reclaim the used moisture by capturing/condensing it, separating contaminants via filtration, and recycling the recovered water to minimize net water use.
included_members.label: Aerosol cleaning with moisture capture and recycling
included_members.description: Use a fine airborne moisture phase to mobilize and lift soil from textiles, then reclaim the used moisture by capturing/condensing it, separating contaminants via filtration, and recycling the recovered water to minimize net water use.
included_members.explanation: M141 captures and reclaims moisture for reuse, matching Closed-Loop Fluid Recovery & Regeneration.

included_members.abstraction: Feedback-controlled water treatment and reuse management: Use sensing-based evaluation and automated control logic to assess treated water condition and dynamically adjust treatment intensity, timing, and reuse/return decisions to maintain acceptable quality while minimizing water use.

included_members.abstraction: Closed-loop wash water regeneration: Captures used wash water, routes it through a staged purification sequence, and returns the regenerated water to the washing process to enable reuse across cycles and reduce fresh water input.

included_members.description: Captures used wash water, routes it through a staged purification sequence, and returns the regenerated water to the washing process to enable reuse across cycles and reduce fresh water input.

included_members.idea_text: A specialized tumbling drum system where clothes are cleaned with a mixture of tiny, reusable cryogel granules. These granules gently abrade the fabric, absorbing oils, dirt, and odor molecules. After the cycle, the granules are separated from the clothes, cleaned (e.g., by vacuuming or solvent bath), and reused, with no water used in the garment cleaning process itself.
included_members.abstraction: Medium separation and regeneration loop: A subsystem that extracts the reusable cleaning medium from textiles, separates and removes collected soils/contaminants from that medium, and restores the medium’s cleaning capacity so it can be recirculated, minimizing water use and waste discharge.
included_members.label: Medium separation and regeneration loop
included_members.description: A subsystem that extracts the reusable cleaning medium from textiles, separates and removes collected soils/contaminants from that medium, and restores the medium’s cleaning capacity so it can be recirculated, minimizing water use and waste discharge.
included_members.explanation: Separating soils from the cleaning medium and restoring its capacity for recirculation matches closed-loop recovery and regeneration.

included_members.idea_text: A laundry drum or chamber equipped with high-efficiency vacuum nozzles and brushes. Clothes are tumbled while a powerful vacuum system actively lifts and extracts dust, lint, pet hair, and superficial dry dirt from the fabric. This process also helps remove airborne particles and can extend the life of garments between full wet washes.
included_members.abstraction: Contaminant separation and removable capture module: A subsystem that separates contaminants from the working stream (air or water), prevents them from re-entering circulation, and accumulates them in a removable/emptyable collection space.
included_members.label: Contaminant separation and removable capture module
included_members.description: A subsystem that separates contaminants from the working stream (air or water), prevents them from re-entering circulation, and accumulates them in a removable/emptyable collection space.
included_members.explanation: Focuses on separating contaminants from the working stream and accumulating them for removal to enable circulation and reuse, aligning with fluid recovery and regeneration.

included_members.idea_text: An advanced washing machine that incorporates an electrocoagulation system into its water purification loop. After a minimal initial wash with water, the greywater is treated with electrocoagulation to rapidly aggregate and remove dirt, dyes, and other contaminants. This pre-treatment significantly reduces the load on subsequent filtration, allowing the water to be recycled and reused much more efficiently for consecutive washes, minimizing fresh water intake.
included_members.abstraction: Low-water prewash soil removal with internal reuse: Introduce an initial, minimal-water cleaning step that mechanically dislodges and concentrates bulk soils, then routes that same small water volume through treatment and back into the wash process to reduce total freshwater input.
included_members.label: Low-water prewash soil removal with internal reuse
included_members.description: Introduce an initial, minimal-water cleaning step that mechanically dislodges and concentrates bulk soils, then routes that same small water volume through treatment and back into the wash process to reduce total freshwater input.
included_members.explanation: Routes low-volume wash water through treatment and back into the wash process, establishing a closed-loop internal reuse system.

included_members.idea_text: An advanced washing machine that incorporates an electrocoagulation system into its water purification loop. After a minimal initial wash with water, the greywater is treated with electrocoagulation to rapidly aggregate and remove dirt, dyes, and other contaminants. This pre-treatment significantly reduces the load on subsequent filtration, allowing the water to be recycled and reused much more efficiently for consecutive washes, minimizing fresh water intake.
included_members.abstraction: Active contaminant coagulation for easy separation: Use an externally driven physicochemical process to destabilize and aggregate dispersed laundry contaminants into larger clumps (flocs), making them simpler to remove from the wash water and enabling effective cleaning with less water.
included_members.label: Active contaminant coagulation for easy separation
included_members.description: Use an externally driven physicochemical process to destabilize and aggregate dispersed laundry contaminants into larger clumps (flocs), making them simpler to remove from the wash water and enabling effective cleaning with less water.
included_members.explanation: Aggregates dispersed contaminants into flocs to facilitate easier removal from wash water, a key step in fluid purification and recovery.

included_members.abstraction: Upfront contaminant agglomeration for easier separation: Pre-treat the wash stream to transform small, dissolved, or fine contaminants into larger, more separable forms so downstream removal can be done with simpler, smaller, or less frequent filtration/polishing, reducing overall water and processing demand.
included_members.label: Upfront contaminant agglomeration for easier separation
included_members.description: Pre-treat the wash stream to transform small, dissolved, or fine contaminants into larger, more separable forms so downstream removal can be done with simpler, smaller, or less frequent filtration/polishing, reducing overall water and processing demand.
included_members.explanation: Pre-treats the wash stream to agglomerate contaminants for downstream filtration and polishing, directly enabling wash fluid regeneration.

included_members.idea_text: A specialized laundry chamber or drum designed with precisely positioned nozzles that generate high-velocity, controlled air vortices around and through the garments. These aerodynamic forces would gently lift and carry away dry dust, lint, pet hair, and superficial particulate dirt from fabric fibers, collecting them in a filter system, effectively de-soiling clothes without any water.
included_members.abstraction: Directed contaminant airflow capture and filtration: Create controlled flow paths that extract contaminant-laden air from the cleaning process and route it through dedicated separation/filtration stages, where particulates (and optionally odors) are retained before the air is released or recirculated.
included_members.label: Directed contaminant airflow capture and filtration
included_members.description: Create controlled flow paths that extract contaminant-laden air from the cleaning process and route it through dedicated separation/filtration stages, where particulates (and optionally odors) are retained before the air is released or recirculated.
included_members.explanation: Captures and filters contaminant-laden air before recirculating it, aligning with the concept of loop recovery and purification.

included_members.idea_text: Develop a cleaning system that introduces microscopic, fabric-safe magnetic particles (e.g., in a fine mist or dry powder form) engineered to selectively adhere to dirt, oils, and odor-causing compounds on garments. After a brief tumbling period to ensure contact, a powerful, oscillating magnetic field is applied to pull these dirt-laden magnetic particles out of the fabric and into a collection chamber for separation and potential reuse.
included_members.abstraction: Medium separation and regeneration loop: A subsystem that extracts the reusable cleaning medium from textiles, separates and removes collected soils/contaminants from that medium, and restores the medium’s cleaning capacity so it can be recirculated, minimizing water use and waste discharge.
included_members.label: Medium separation and regeneration loop
included_members.description: A subsystem that extracts the reusable cleaning medium from textiles, separates and removes collected soils/contaminants from that medium, and restores the medium’s cleaning capacity so it can be recirculated, minimizing water use and waste discharge.
included_members.explanation: Separates soils from the reusable cleaning medium and restores its capacity so it can be continuously recirculated.

included_members.idea_text: Design a cleaning chamber where clothes are gently suspended in a minimal volume of water or a specialized, low-surface-tension cleaning solution. A system of diffusers beneath the garments introduces precisely controlled, pulsed streams of fine air or inert gas bubbles. These bubbles percolate through the fabric, creating a gentle "scrubbing" action that dislodges dirt and impurities, which are then collected from the circulating minimal liquid.
included_members.abstraction: Minimal-liquid circulation with contaminant separation: Use a very small amount of cleaning fluid in a continuous flow over/through the laundry, then collect it, remove dislodged soils via separation/filtration, and recirculate the cleaned fluid to sustain cleaning performance with low water use.
included_members.label: Minimal-liquid circulation with contaminant separation
included_members.description: Use a very small amount of cleaning fluid in a continuous flow over/through the laundry, then collect it, remove dislodged soils via separation/filtration, and recirculate the cleaned fluid to sustain cleaning performance with low water use.
included_members.explanation: Describes collecting, filtering, and recirculating cleaning fluid to reduce water usage, fitting the closed-loop recovery cluster.

included_members.idea_text: A specialized washing unit where clothes are suspended in a minimal amount of slightly conductive water or a weak electrolyte solution. The chamber incorporates alternating cation and anion exchange membranes. By applying an electric current, charged dirt particles (ions) and dissolved impurities are drawn out of the fabric and across the membranes, leaving cleaner fabric and significantly purified water for near-complete reuse within the closed system.
included_members.abstraction: Minimal-bath closed-loop recirculating wash system: Use a small-volume wash chamber that keeps textiles engaged with a limited liquid bath while continuously circulating that liquid through a purification step and returning it to the chamber, enabling repeated reuse of the same water with minimal fresh-water makeup.
included_members.label: Minimal-bath closed-loop recirculating wash system
included_members.description: Use a small-volume wash chamber that keeps textiles engaged with a limited liquid bath while continuously circulating that liquid through a purification step and returning it to the chamber, enabling repeated reuse of the same water with minimal fresh-water makeup.
included_members.explanation: Uses a closed-loop system to continuously purify and recirculate a small volume wash bath.

included_members.idea_text: A specialized washing unit where clothes are suspended in a minimal amount of slightly conductive water or a weak electrolyte solution. The chamber incorporates alternating cation and anion exchange membranes. By applying an electric current, charged dirt particles (ions) and dissolved impurities are drawn out of the fabric and across the membranes, leaving cleaner fabric and significantly purified water for near-complete reuse within the closed system.
included_members.abstraction: Selective barrier-driven separation and isolation: Use selective barriers to actively direct and partition dissolved contaminants out of the wash fluid into a separate compartment, preventing back-mixing and enabling concentrated removal so the same water can be reused with less fresh input.
included_members.label: Selective barrier-driven separation and isolation
included_members.description: Use selective barriers to actively direct and partition dissolved contaminants out of the wash fluid into a separate compartment, preventing back-mixing and enabling concentrated removal so the same water can be reused with less fresh input.
included_members.explanation: Partitions dissolved contaminants out of the fluid to enable the reuse of the same water.

included_members.idea_text: Develop cleaning agents or fabric coatings containing embedded or surface-applied smart polymers. When triggered (e.g., by a slight temperature change or pH adjustment in a low-humidity chamber with minimal mist), these polymers swell, physically pushing dirt and grime out of the fabric pores. Upon a reverse trigger, they contract, squeezing out any trapped impurities or dirty water, which is then collected, significantly reducing water usage for cleaning and rinsing.
included_members.abstraction: Extract-and-separate contaminant capture loop: Mechanisms that remove soil-laden matter from textiles via controlled extraction (e.g., suction/flow), immediately capture it in a closed pathway, and perform separation/filtration to isolate contaminants for containment, disposal, or potential reuse of the cleaned medium.
included_members.label: Extract-and-separate contaminant capture loop
included_members.description: Mechanisms that remove soil-laden matter from textiles via controlled extraction (e.g., suction/flow), immediately capture it in a closed pathway, and perform separation/filtration to isolate contaminants for containment, disposal, or potential reuse of the cleaned medium.
included_members.explanation: Captures extracted soil in a closed pathway and filters it to reuse the cleaned medium.

included_members.idea_text: A washing device featuring a textured internal surface or specialized micro-channels. Garments are laid flat or gently rolled across this surface while a very thin, continuously flowing film of water or cleaning solution is introduced. The micro-scale geometry of the surface generates localized fluid shear forces that effectively "peel" and dislodge surface dirt and oils from the fabric with an extremely low volume of liquid, which is then filtered and recirculated.
included_members.abstraction: Minimal-liquid circulation with contaminant separation: Use a very small amount of cleaning fluid in a continuous flow over/through the laundry, then collect it, remove dislodged soils via separation/filtration, and recirculate the cleaned fluid to sustain cleaning performance with low water use.
included_members.label: Minimal-liquid circulation with contaminant separation
included_members.description: Use a very small amount of cleaning fluid in a continuous flow over/through the laundry, then collect it, remove dislodged soils via separation/filtration, and recirculate the cleaned fluid to sustain cleaning performance with low water use.
included_members.explanation: Collects, filters, and recirculates cleaning fluid, enabling closed-loop recovery.

included_members.idea_text: A compact garment cleaning appliance that uses a targeted, re-circulating vapor of a fabric-safe, low-boiling-point solvent (e.g., a modified alcohol or fluorocarbon). Clothes, or specific stained areas, are exposed to this vapor. The vapor condenses on the cooler fabric, dissolves oils and grime, and then re-evaporates, carrying the contaminants away to a recovery and purification system, leaving no residue and requiring no water for the cleaning process.
included_members.abstraction: Closed-loop solvent recovery and purification: A recirculating fluid-management subsystem that captures used cleaning solvent (vapor and/or liquid), separates and removes contaminants, restores solvent quality via regeneration, and returns it to the cleaning process to minimize fresh solvent and water demand.
included_members.label: Closed-loop solvent recovery and purification
included_members.description: A recirculating fluid-management subsystem that captures used cleaning solvent (vapor and/or liquid), separates and removes contaminants, restores solvent quality via regeneration, and returns it to the cleaning process to minimize fresh solvent and water demand.
included_members.explanation: Describes a closed-loop system for capturing, purifying, and returning solvent to minimize fresh demand.

included_members.idea_text: A sealed garment cabinet containing regenerable desiccant materials (e.g., advanced zeolites or MOFs) and a fan. Air is circulated through the garments and then over the desiccant bed. The desiccant actively pulls moisture (and dissolved body oils/odors) directly from the fabric into the air stream, and then adsorbs it. This dry extraction process cleanses and deodorizes garments without the use of water. The desiccant can then be heated to release the dirty moisture for disposal and regenerate for reuse.
included_members.abstraction: Sorbent regeneration and concentrated waste removal: Restore sorbent reuse by cycling operating conditions (e.g., heat and/or pressure/flow changes) to release previously captured moisture/contaminants, then separate and collect the desorbed output as a concentrated waste stream for removal or further treatment.
included_members.label: Sorbent regeneration and concentrated waste removal
included_members.description: Restore sorbent reuse by cycling operating conditions (e.g., heat and/or pressure/flow changes) to release previously captured moisture/contaminants, then separate and collect the desorbed output as a concentrated waste stream for removal or further treatment.
included_members.explanation: Focuses on regenerating a capture medium (sorbent) by removing captured waste so the medium can be continuously reused.

included_members.idea_text: A sealed garment cabinet containing regenerable desiccant materials (e.g., advanced zeolites or MOFs) and a fan. Air is circulated through the garments and then over the desiccant bed. The desiccant actively pulls moisture (and dissolved body oils/odors) directly from the fabric into the air stream, and then adsorbs it. This dry extraction process cleanses and deodorizes garments without the use of water. The desiccant can then be heated to release the dirty moisture for disposal and regenerate for reuse.
included_members.abstraction: Recirculating airflow with sorbent filtration for dry cleaning: Use a controlled, often enclosed, airflow loop that repeatedly passes air over/through garments to lift moisture and volatile soils, then routes that air through an adsorption/filtration medium to capture contaminants before recirculating the cleaned air back to the textiles.
included_members.label: Recirculating airflow with sorbent filtration for dry cleaning
included_members.description: Use a controlled, often enclosed, airflow loop that repeatedly passes air over/through garments to lift moisture and volatile soils, then routes that air through an adsorption/filtration medium to capture contaminants before recirculating the cleaned air back to the textiles.
included_members.explanation: Uses a recirculating airflow loop that continuously cleans the air via filtration before returning it to the textiles.

included_members.idea_text: A system where garments are briefly immersed in a minimal volume of a low-viscosity, fabric-safe MR fluid. A pulsed magnetic field is then applied, causing the fluid to momentarily thicken around the fabric fibers, effectively encapsulating and mechanically stressing embedded dirt and oil particles. When the field is removed, the fluid instantly thins, releasing the loosened dirt, which is then carried away by filtration. The fluid is continuously recycled and purified for subsequent uses with minimal loss and no water.
included_members.abstraction: Closed-loop wash-fluid recovery and purification: Continuously capture used or recovered liquid from the process, remove suspended and dissolved contaminants through in-line separation/filtration, and return the cleaned working fluid back to the system for reuse to reduce fresh water demand.
included_members.label: Closed-loop wash-fluid recovery and purification
included_members.description: Continuously capture used or recovered liquid from the process, remove suspended and dissolved contaminants through in-line separation/filtration, and return the cleaned working fluid back to the system for reuse to reduce fresh water demand.
included_members.explanation: Capturing and purifying used liquid to recirculate as clean working fluid perfectly matches closed-loop fluid recovery and regeneration.

included_members.idea_text: A specialized, highly reusable sheet or pad made from a superhydrophilic, finely textured material designed to be placed in a tumbling dryer or a dedicated refresh cabinet with clothes. During a brief cycle with a very fine, minimal mist of water, this sheet actively attracts and captures body oils, dissolved dirt, and fine particulate matter released from the garments. The superhydrophilic material "wicks" and holds these contaminants, effectively cleaning the clothes with minimal water, and the sheet is then rinsed clean for reuse.
included_members.abstraction: Closed-loop handling and regeneration of contaminant-capture media: Mechanisms that collect the used contaminant-removal medium after it has captured soils, then process it (clean, regenerate, or safely dispose) so the medium can be returned to service or handled with minimal water and environmental burden.
included_members.label: Closed-loop handling and regeneration of contaminant-capture media
included_members.description: Mechanisms that collect the used contaminant-removal medium after it has captured soils, then process it (clean, regenerate, or safely dispose) so the medium can be returned to service or handled with minimal water and environmental burden.
included_members.explanation: Collecting, cleaning, and regenerating used contaminant-removal media for return to service is closed-loop recovery and regeneration.

included_members.idea_text: A controlled chamber system that applies a fine, non-toxic, biodegradable, and fabric-safe "bio-slime" (e.g., a hydrogel-based polymer with specific adhesive properties) mist onto clothes. This slime is engineered to be slightly adhesive to dirt and odor molecules. After a short dwell time, a second stage triggers a controlled 'shedding' or breakdown of the slime (e.g., via a pH change or mild vibration), causing it to detach from the fabric, carrying the trapped dirt and odors with it, into a collection system. The slime is then processed for disposal or regeneration, leaving clean, residue-free clothes with minimal water usage.
included_members.abstraction: Closed-loop handling and regeneration of contaminant-capture media: Mechanisms that collect the used contaminant-removal medium after it has captured soils, then process it (clean, regenerate, or safely dispose) so the medium can be returned to service or handled with minimal water and environmental burden.
included_members.label: Closed-loop handling and regeneration of contaminant-capture media
included_members.description: Mechanisms that collect the used contaminant-removal medium after it has captured soils, then process it (clean, regenerate, or safely dispose) so the medium can be returned to service or handled with minimal water and environmental burden.
included_members.explanation: Processing and regenerating used capture media to return it to service matches closed-loop recovery.

included_members.idea_text: A minimal-water wash system where clothes are immersed in a very small volume of water containing a low concentration of cleaning agents. High-frequency acoustic transducers are precisely arrayed to generate acoustic radiation forces that gently 'push' and aggregate dirt particles within the water towards a specific collection zone or filter, without requiring bulk fluid flow or mechanical agitation of the clothes. This allows for highly efficient dirt removal from the water, enabling near-complete water recirculation and minimal fresh water input for effective cleaning.
included_members.abstraction: Localized contaminant capture for solvent reuse: Create a directed collection point that receives concentrated/aggregated contaminants and retains them via filtration or trapping, separating soil from the wash liquid so the remaining solvent can be reused with less fresh water.
included_members.label: Localized contaminant capture for solvent reuse
included_members.description: Create a directed collection point that receives concentrated/aggregated contaminants and retains them via filtration or trapping, separating soil from the wash liquid so the remaining solvent can be reused with less fresh water.
included_members.explanation: Separating soil from wash liquid via filtration so the solvent can be reused describes closed-loop fluid recovery.

included_members.idea_text: A washing machine integrated with a membrane distillation unit. After an initial minimal-water wash, the greywater is fed into the membrane distillation system. Water vapor passes through the hydrophobic membrane, leaving all dissolved and suspended contaminants in the concentrated brine. This purified water is then condensed and immediately recycled for the next wash cycle, achieving ultra-high water recovery and significantly reducing fresh water intake.
included_members.abstraction: Low-water prewash soil removal with internal reuse: Introduce an initial, minimal-water cleaning step that mechanically dislodges and concentrates bulk soils, then routes that same small water volume through treatment and back into the wash process to reduce total freshwater input.
included_members.label: Low-water prewash soil removal with internal reuse
included_members.description: Introduce an initial, minimal-water cleaning step that mechanically dislodges and concentrates bulk soils, then routes that same small water volume through treatment and back into the wash process to reduce total freshwater input.
included_members.explanation: Routing wash water through treatment for internal reuse matches closed-loop fluid recovery and regeneration.

included_members.idea_text: A washing machine integrated with a membrane distillation unit. After an initial minimal-water wash, the greywater is fed into the membrane distillation system. Water vapor passes through the hydrophobic membrane, leaving all dissolved and suspended contaminants in the concentrated brine. This purified water is then condensed and immediately recycled for the next wash cycle, achieving ultra-high water recovery and significantly reducing fresh water intake.
included_members.abstraction: Membrane-driven water extraction from laundry wastewater: Use a selective membrane and a cross-membrane driving force (e.g., vapor pressure or osmotic pressure gradient) to pull water through while blocking dissolved and particulate contaminants, enabling water recovery and reuse with minimal fresh-water input.
included_members.label: Membrane-driven water extraction from laundry wastewater
included_members.description: Use a selective membrane and a cross-membrane driving force (e.g., vapor pressure or osmotic pressure gradient) to pull water through while blocking dissolved and particulate contaminants, enabling water recovery and reuse with minimal fresh-water input.
included_members.explanation: Membrane-driven water extraction for recovery and reuse directly fits closed-loop fluid recovery and regeneration.

included_members.idea_text: A washing machine integrated with a membrane distillation unit. After an initial minimal-water wash, the greywater is fed into the membrane distillation system. Water vapor passes through the hydrophobic membrane, leaving all dissolved and suspended contaminants in the concentrated brine. This purified water is then condensed and immediately recycled for the next wash cycle, achieving ultra-high water recovery and significantly reducing fresh water intake.
included_members.abstraction: Closed-loop wash-water recirculation: Recover water from the process, purify it, and route it back into the wash cycle through a controlled circulation loop to reduce or eliminate fresh make-up water.
included_members.label: Closed-loop wash-water recirculation
included_members.description: Recover water from the process, purify it, and route it back into the wash cycle through a controlled circulation loop to reduce or eliminate fresh make-up water.
included_members.explanation: Purifying and routing wash water back into the cycle is the definition of closed-loop fluid recovery.

included_members.idea_text: A washing machine integrated with a membrane distillation unit. After an initial minimal-water wash, the greywater is fed into the membrane distillation system. Water vapor passes through the hydrophobic membrane, leaving all dissolved and suspended contaminants in the concentrated brine. This purified water is then condensed and immediately recycled for the next wash cycle, achieving ultra-high water recovery and significantly reducing fresh water intake.
included_members.abstraction: Concentrate isolation and retention: Separate and contain the non-recoverable concentrated waste stream from the cleaning loop so it does not remix with reclaimed water, enabling periodic removal/disposal while preserving water quality.
included_members.label: Concentrate isolation and retention
included_members.description: Separate and contain the non-recoverable concentrated waste stream from the cleaning loop so it does not remix with reclaimed water, enabling periodic removal/disposal while preserving water quality.
included_members.explanation: Isolating concentrate from the cleaning loop ensures the reclaimed fluid is pure, a key component of fluid regeneration.

included_members.idea_text: A garment refreshing cabinet that utilizes a bed of regenerable, fabric-safe chemical sorbents (e.g., modified amines or Metal-Organic Frameworks). These sorbents are specifically engineered to reversibly bind volatile organic compounds (VOCs) responsible for odors. Air is circulated through the garments and then over the sorbent bed, trapping odors. The sorbent is then periodically regenerated (e.g., by heating or pressure swing), releasing concentrated odors for safe disposal, making this a highly efficient, water-free, and chemical-free deodorization system.
included_members.abstraction: Recirculating airflow with sorbent filtration for dry cleaning: Use a controlled, often enclosed, airflow loop that repeatedly passes air over/through garments to lift moisture and volatile soils, then routes that air through an adsorption/filtration medium to capture contaminants before recirculating the cleaned air back to the textiles.
included_members.label: Recirculating airflow with sorbent filtration for dry cleaning
included_members.description: Use a controlled, often enclosed, airflow loop that repeatedly passes air over/through garments to lift moisture and volatile soils, then routes that air through an adsorption/filtration medium to capture contaminants before recirculating the cleaned air back to the textiles.
included_members.explanation: Recirculating a flow loop of air and filtering it continuously aligns with closed-loop fluid/medium recovery.

included_members.idea_text: A garment cleaning system where a very fine, dry, and biodegradable micro-abrasive powder (e.g., cellulose beads) is gently dusted onto clothes. A precisely controlled, low-power pulsed laser beam then scans the fabric. The laser energy interacts with the micro-abrasive particles, causing them to gently 'lift' or 'etch' away dirt and grime from the fabric surface through localized photomechanical action. The dirty micro-abrasive is then vacuumed away, providing a contactless, water-free cleaning method.
included_members.abstraction: Extract-and-separate contaminant capture loop: Mechanisms that remove soil-laden matter from textiles via controlled extraction (e.g., suction/flow), immediately capture it in a closed pathway, and perform separation/filtration to isolate contaminants for containment, disposal, or potential reuse of the cleaned medium.
included_members.label: Extract-and-separate contaminant capture loop
included_members.description: Mechanisms that remove soil-laden matter from textiles via controlled extraction (e.g., suction/flow), immediately capture it in a closed pathway, and perform separation/filtration to isolate contaminants for containment, disposal, or potential reuse of the cleaned medium.
included_members.explanation: Extracting, separating, and isolating contaminants for the potential reuse of the cleaned medium fits the closed-loop recovery and regeneration cluster.

included_members.idea_text: A sealed chamber where garments are exposed to a precise, low-temperature, recycled carrier gas containing a non-toxic, fabric-safe binding agent. This agent selectively vaporizes, diffuses into the fabric, adsorbs to dirt and odor molecules, and then is carried away by the gas stream to a separation and recovery unit. The carrier gas and binding agent are continuously purified and reused, effectively "chromatographically eluting" dirt and odors from the fabric without water.
included_members.abstraction: Medium separation and regeneration loop: A subsystem that extracts the reusable cleaning medium from textiles, separates and removes collected soils/contaminants from that medium, and restores the medium’s cleaning capacity so it can be recirculated, minimizing water use and waste discharge.
included_members.label: Medium separation and regeneration loop
included_members.description: A subsystem that extracts the reusable cleaning medium from textiles, separates and removes collected soils/contaminants from that medium, and restores the medium’s cleaning capacity so it can be recirculated, minimizing water use and waste discharge.
included_members.explanation: Separating collected soils from the medium and restoring its capacity for recirculation is the definition of closed-loop fluid recovery and regeneration.

included_members.idea_text: A laundry appliance featuring a series of rotating polymer rollers whose surfaces are engineered to have a higher affinity for common dirt and oil molecules than for fabric fibers. As garments pass through, these rollers gently contact the fabric, transferring dirt and oils from the clothes onto their own surfaces. A secondary, integrated mechanism continuously cleans the rollers (e.g., with a scraper or micro-solvent spray which is then recovered), enabling continuous dirt removal from clothes without water.
included_members.abstraction: Continuous cleaning-surface regeneration: A functional subsystem that continually restores the contaminant-receiving surface during operation by removing accumulated soils and routing the extracted contaminants into a controlled collection or recovery path, so the surface remains effective without requiring additional water.
included_members.label: Continuous cleaning-surface regeneration
included_members.description: A functional subsystem that continually restores the contaminant-receiving surface during operation by removing accumulated soils and routing the extracted contaminants into a controlled collection or recovery path, so the surface remains effective without requiring additional water.
included_members.explanation: Continually restoring the contaminant-receiving surface during operation is a form of cleaning medium regeneration and recovery.

included_members.idea_text: A low-water washing system that uses a mild, biodegradable solution containing engineered humic acid analogues or naturally derived humic substances. These compounds act as powerful chelating and dispersing agents, effectively binding to dirt, oils, and metal ions embedded in fabric. This complexation process makes the contaminants easier to rinse away with a minimal amount of water, which is then purified and recycled through a system optimized to separate the humic-dirt complexes.
included_members.abstraction: Closed-loop rinse-water separation and reuse: Use a cyclic process that selectively separates bound contaminants from used rinse water, then returns the cleaned water (and any still-effective wash chemistry) back into the laundering steps to minimize total fresh-water input.
included_members.label: Closed-loop rinse-water separation and reuse
included_members.description: Use a cyclic process that selectively separates bound contaminants from used rinse water, then returns the cleaned water (and any still-effective wash chemistry) back into the laundering steps to minimize total fresh-water input.
included_members.explanation: Involves closed-loop separation and reuse of rinse water and chemistry to minimize fresh water input.

included_members.idea_text: A sealed garment cabinet that uses a small, contained reservoir of water. This water is rapidly heated to generate superheated, dry steam (vapor without liquid droplets). This superheated steam is circulated through the garments, effectively sterilizing, deodorizing, and loosening superficial dirt and oils through thermal shock and vapor action. The steam then cools, condenses, and is immediately collected, filtered, and returned to the reservoir for continuous reuse, achieving powerful cleaning with extremely low water replenishment.
included_members.abstraction: Closed-loop wash-fluid recovery and purification: Continuously capture used or recovered liquid from the process, remove suspended and dissolved contaminants through in-line separation/filtration, and return the cleaned working fluid back to the system for reuse to reduce fresh water demand.
included_members.label: Closed-loop wash-fluid recovery and purification
included_members.description: Continuously capture used or recovered liquid from the process, remove suspended and dissolved contaminants through in-line separation/filtration, and return the cleaned working fluid back to the system for reuse to reduce fresh water demand.
included_members.explanation: Continuously captures, purifies, and recirculates wash fluid to reduce fresh water demand.

included_members.idea_text: Garments are treated with a dissolvable or detachable nanocoating that has a stronger affinity for dirt/oils than for fabric fibers. After wear, the garments are placed in a gentle tumbling drum or cabinet. A mild, fabric-safe trigger (e.g., a specific light wavelength, a slight humidity change, or a very mild vibration) causes the nanocoating to rapidly delaminate or de-bond from the fabric, encapsulating and releasing the accumulated dirt. The shed nanocoating and dirt particles are then collected by a vacuum and filter system, leaving clean fabric with no water.
included_members.abstraction: Extract-and-separate contaminant capture loop: Mechanisms that remove soil-laden matter from textiles via controlled extraction (e.g., suction/flow), immediately capture it in a closed pathway, and perform separation/filtration to isolate contaminants for containment, disposal, or potential reuse of the cleaned medium.
included_members.label: Extract-and-separate contaminant capture loop
included_members.description: Mechanisms that remove soil-laden matter from textiles via controlled extraction (e.g., suction/flow), immediately capture it in a closed pathway, and perform separation/filtration to isolate contaminants for containment, disposal, or potential reuse of the cleaned medium.
included_members.explanation: Captures soil-laden matter in a closed loop for separation, filtration, and potential reuse.

included_members.idea_text: A washing machine integrated with a forward osmosis system. After an initial, minimal-water wash cycle, the greywater (feed solution) is pumped to one side of an FO membrane. A highly concentrated, reusable draw solution is on the other side. Clean water is naturally pulled from the greywater through the membrane, leaving all contaminants and dirt in the concentrated feed solution, and the purified water is then recycled back into the wash system for continuous reuse, drastically reducing fresh water consumption.
included_members.abstraction: Low-water prewash soil removal with internal reuse: Introduce an initial, minimal-water cleaning step that mechanically dislodges and concentrates bulk soils, then routes that same small water volume through treatment and back into the wash process to reduce total freshwater input.
included_members.label: Low-water prewash soil removal with internal reuse
included_members.description: Introduce an initial, minimal-water cleaning step that mechanically dislodges and concentrates bulk soils, then routes that same small water volume through treatment and back into the wash process to reduce total freshwater input.
included_members.explanation: Reuses a small water volume by routing it back through the wash process, minimizing fresh water.

included_members.idea_text: A washing machine integrated with a forward osmosis system. After an initial, minimal-water wash cycle, the greywater (feed solution) is pumped to one side of an FO membrane. A highly concentrated, reusable draw solution is on the other side. Clean water is naturally pulled from the greywater through the membrane, leaving all contaminants and dirt in the concentrated feed solution, and the purified water is then recycled back into the wash system for continuous reuse, drastically reducing fresh water consumption.

included_members.explanation: Extracts water via a membrane for recovery and reuse, fitting closed-loop regeneration.
